main_dirt.bias_notes: A 1-mile dirt oval with a 990-foot home straight. The main track alternates Thoroughbred races with Quarter Horse dashes, which compacts the inside rail cushion and frequently creates a fast early speed ('E') rail bias in sprints (5F-6.5F) and 1-mile routes. Deep closers ('C') require a genuine pace meltdown to win on fast dirt.
main_dirt.post_bias: In dirt sprints (5F to 6.5F), inside and middle posts (1–5) hold a distinct advantage to secure early position and save ground into the turn. In 1 1/16M dirt routes, inside posts (1–4) avoid wide trips.

main_turf.bias_notes: Set inside the main dirt track, this tighter 7/8-mile turf course strongly rewards tactical speed ('P') and ground-saving inside trips. In 1-Mile and 1 1/16-Mile turf routes, the short run to the first turn heavily penalizes wide-drawn runners. Deep closers ('Swoopers') frequently struggle to make up ground on the tight turns.
main_turf.post_bias: INSIDE TURF BIAS: Inside posts (1–4) hold a strong advantage. Wide draws (8+) in two-turn turf routes face an automatic ground-loss penalty due to the short run into the tight first bend.

handicapping_angles.kentucky_shipper_class_elevator: Horseshoe Indianapolis is a primary landing spot for horses dropping out of the ultra-competitive Kentucky circuit (Churchill Downs, Keeneland, Ellis Park, Turfway Park). Aggressively upgrade Kentucky shippers (+3.5 pts), as they typically hold a massive inherent class edge over local Midwest form lines.
handicapping_angles.indiana_bred_restricted_class_filter: Indiana-Bred (IN-Bred) restricted races carry lower speed figure pars than Open company. When an IN-Bred runner steps up into Open Allowance or Open Stakes, apply a -3.0 point class discount unless possessing dominant speed figures.
handicapping_angles.quarter_horse_rail_compaction_speed_bias: Because the track alternates Thoroughbred races with Quarter Horse dashes, the inside rail cushion is heavily packed. On dry afternoons, early speed ('E') drawn inside (Posts 1–4) dominates dirt sprints at a nearly 45% win rate.
handicapping_angles.indiana_derby_and_oaks_stakes_class: During the Grade 3 Indiana Derby ($300k+) and Indiana Oaks meeting in July, track class elevates to Tier 1.5 level. Factor in higher speed par offsets for Derby day feature races.
